name: Saint Barthélemy
rule: The current territorial Environment Code, consolidated after 12 March 2026, restricts living specimens under Article 32-17; its plant annex concerns living plants, fruiting bodies and propagules. That invasive-species restriction does not establish a permit duty for manufactured, non-living sencha. Separate national plant-health controls still apply through Code rural L272-11-1; the applicable finished-tea import schedule has not been established.
personalMailApplicability: Environmental living-specimen controls do not resolve the separate plant-health conditions for Japanese retail tea sent by post. No current territorial manufactured-tea postal clearance was verified.
authority: Saint Barthélemy territorial government/ATE; French Code rural and plant-health authority
remainingQuestion: Need the operative plant-health commodity schedule under Code rural L272-11-1/L271-5 to L271-8 for finished Japanese tea. The current 2026 Environment Code has now been read: its living-specimen restriction is not itself the missing manufactured-food classification.
researchAttempts: Reviewed ATE territorial invasive-plant rules, native-flora guidance and plant authorization forms; no processed-tea or personal-post provision found.

Second review searched 2025/2026 local tea exclusions. The 2025 ministry overseas instruction explicitly excludes Saint Barthélemy/Saint Martin regulations from its analysis; it does not extend a mainland exemption.

Retrieved the official 199-page Environment Code via the territorial website’s March 2026 consolidation link. Read Articles 32-1 to 32-28 and the Article 32-17 plant annex: the invasive-species prohibition concerns living specimens. Separately read current Code rural L272-1, L272-3 and L272-11-1. Environmental scope is now clear but does not establish the applicable national agricultural import schedule; no inferred blanket tea ban or clearance.
permitFreeReason: Need the operative plant-health commodity schedule under Code rural L272-11-1/L271-5 to L271-8 for finished Japanese tea. The current 2026 Environment Code has now been read: its living-specimen restriction is not itself the missing manufactured-food classification.

name: Saint Martin (French part)
rule: Saint Martin is outside the EU plant-health territory. A Dutch NPPO country sheet lists specific dried plant goods needing certification, but does not list tea and dates its substantive rules to 2012; that cannot verify the present Japanese postal route. Current Code rural L273-6-2 expressly applies the overseas plant-health framework in L271-5 to L271-8 to Saint Martin; this confirms the governing framework but does not supply the missing commodity-level finished-tea decision.
personalMailApplicability: No current local manufactured-tea/personal-post confirmation; do not use mainland French rules automatically.
authority: Netherlands NVWA country requirements for Saint Martin; French plant-health law
remainingQuestion: Need a current Saint Martin commodity schedule and confirmation that direct Japanese finished tea is outside certificate controls. The available NVWA country sheet reflects 2012 substantive rules and does not list tea; it is insufficient evidence of present territorial rules.
researchAttempts: Reviewed the full NVWA Saint Martin country sheet, including its 2012/2013 revision history and third-country plant-product list; searched French local import guidance. Current tea-specific scope remains unverified.

Second review searched 2025/2026 local tea exclusions. The 2025 ministry overseas instruction explicitly excludes Saint Barthélemy/Saint Martin regulations from its analysis; it does not extend a mainland exemption.

Read current Code rural L273-1 to L273-7, including L273-6-2’s express extension of the overseas plant-health framework. This strengthens the legal-framework evidence but is not a tea-specific schedule or a personal-post exemption.
permitFreeReason: Need a current Saint Martin commodity schedule and confirmation that direct Japanese finished tea is outside certificate controls. The available NVWA country sheet reflects 2012 substantive rules and does not list tea; it is insufficient evidence of present territorial rules.
